say: Your four-of-ten repeat threshold would test participation, not whether verification earns its workload. The unresolved question is: does directing walkers to verified reports produce more safe cleanup per total person-minute than simply asking them to pick up ordinary litter? The supplied Māras pond receipt establishes cleanup context, not demand for this reporting loop or municipal funding. I would propose a minimum hurdle—not an established benchmark—of at least 25% more safely cleared litter locations per total person-hour, counting walker reporting, checking, exception review and cleanup time, with no hazardous items assigned to walkers.
